//! The Wasmi virtual machine definitions.
//!
//! These closely mirror the WebAssembly specification definitions.
//! The overall structure is heavily inspired by the `wasmtime` virtual
//! machine architecture.
//!
//! # Example
//!
//! The following example shows a "Hello, World!"-like example of creating
//! a Wasm module from some initial `.wat` contents, defining a simple host
//! function and calling the exported Wasm function.
//!
//! The example was inspired by
//! [Wasmtime's API example](https://docs.rs/wasmtime/0.39.1/wasmtime/).
//!
//! ```
//! use wasmi::*;
//!
//! // In this simple example we are going to compile the below Wasm source,
//! // instantiate a Wasm module from it and call its exported "hello" function.
//! fn main() -> Result<(), wasmi::Error> {
//!     let wasm = r#"
//!         (module
//!             (import "host" "hello" (func $host_hello (param i32)))
//!             (func (export "hello")
//!                 (call $host_hello (i32.const 3))
//!             )
//!         )
//!     "#;
//!     // First step is to create the Wasm execution engine with some config.
//!     //
//!     // In this example we are using the default configuration.
//!     let engine = Engine::default();
//!     // Now we can compile the above Wasm module with the given Wasm source.
//!     let module = Module::new(&engine, wasm)?;
//!
//!     // Wasm objects operate within the context of a Wasm `Store`.
//!     //
//!     // Each `Store` has a type parameter to store host specific data.
//!     // In this example the host state is a simple `u32` type with value `42`.
//!     type HostState = u32;
//!     let mut store = Store::new(&engine, 42);
//!
//!     // A linker can be used to instantiate Wasm modules.
//!     // The job of a linker is to satisfy the Wasm module's imports.
//!     let mut linker = <Linker<HostState>>::new(&engine);
//!     // We are required to define all imports before instantiating a Wasm module.
//!     linker.func_wrap("host", "hello", |caller: Caller<'_, HostState>, param: i32| {
//!         println!("Got {param} from WebAssembly and my host state is: {}", caller.data());
//!     });
//!     let instance = linker.instantiate_and_start(&mut store, &module)?;
//!     // Now we can finally query the exported "hello" function and call it.
//!     instance
//!         .get_typed_func::<(), ()>(&store, "hello")?
//!         .call(&mut store, ())?;
//!     Ok(())
//! }
//! ```
//!
//! # Crate Features
//!
//! | Feature | Crates | Description |
//! |:-:|:--|:--|
//! | `std` | `wasmi`<br>`wasmi_core`<br>`wasmi_ir`<br>`wasmi_collections` | Enables usage of Rust's standard library. This may have some performance advantages when enabled. Disabling this feature makes Wasmi compile on platforms that do not provide Rust's standard library such as many embedded platforms. <br><br> Enabled by default. |
//! | `wat` | `wasmi` | Enables support to parse Wat encoded Wasm modules. <br><br> Enabled by default. |
//! | `simd` | `wasmi`<br>`wasmi_core`<br>`wasmi_ir`<br>`wasmi_cli` | Enables support for the Wasm `simd` and `relaxed-simd` proposals. <br><br> Disabled by default. |
//! | `hash-collections` | `wasmi`<br>`wasmi_collections` | Enables use of hash-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This might yield performance improvements in some use cases. <br><br> Disabled by default. |
//! | `prefer-btree-collections` | `wasmi`<br>`wasmi_collections` | Enforces use of btree-map based collections in Wasmi internals. This may yield performance improvements and memory consumption decreases in some use cases. Also it enables Wasmi to run on platforms that have no random source. <br><br> Disabled by default. |
//! | `extra-checks` | `wasmi` | Enables extra runtime checks in the Wasmi executor. Expected execution overhead is ~20%. Enable this if your focus is on safety. Disable this for maximum execution performance. <br><br> Disabled by default. |

impl Module {
    /// Creates a new Wasm [`Module`] from the given Wasm bytecode buffer.
    ///
    /// # Note
    ///
    /// - This parses, validates and translates the buffered Wasm bytecode.
    /// - The `wasm` may be encoded as WebAssembly binary (`.wasm`) or as
    ///   WebAssembly text format (`.wat`).
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// - If the Wasm bytecode is malformed or fails to validate.
    /// - If the Wasm bytecode violates restrictions
    ///   set in the [`Config`] used by the `engine`.
    /// - If Wasmi cannot translate the Wasm bytecode.
    ///
    /// [`Config`]: crate::Config
    pub fn new(engine: &Engine, wasm: impl AsRef<[u8]>) -> Result<Self, Error> {
        let wasm = wasm.as_ref();
        #[cfg(feature = "wat")]
        let wasm = &wat::parse_bytes(wasm)?[..];
        ModuleParser::new(engine).parse_buffered(wasm)
    }

    /// Creates a new Wasm [`Module`] from the given Wasm bytecode buffer.

    /// # Note

    /// This parses and translates the buffered Wasm bytecode.
    ///
    /// # Safety
    ///
    /// - This does _not_ validate the Wasm bytecode.
    /// - It is the caller's responsibility that the Wasm bytecode is valid.

    /// [`Config`]: crate::Config

        let parser = ModuleParser::new(engine);

```rust
pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> Option<String> {
    let section = self.custom_sections().find(|s| s.name() == "name")?;
    let data = section.data();
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < data.len() {
        let id = *data.get(i)?;
        i += 1;
        let (size, n) = read_uleb(data, i)?;
        i += n;
        let end = i.checked_add(size)?;
        if end > data.len() { return None; }
        if id == 0 {
            // module name subsection: payload is a name
            let (len, n) = read_uleb(data, i)?;
            i += n;
            let start = i.checked_add(len as usize)?;
            let bytes = data.get(i..start)?;
            return String::from_utf8(bytes.to_vec()).ok();
        }
        i = end;
    }
    None
}
```

    pub(crate) fn name(&self) -> Option<String> {

/// Reads an unsigned LEB128 encoded `u32` from `data` starting at `offset`.
fn read_uleb(data: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<(usize, usize)> {
    let mut result: u32 = 0;
    let mut shift = 0;
    let mut i = offset;
    loop {
        let byte = *data.get(i)?;
        i += 1;
        let low = u32::from(byte & 0x7f);
        result = result.checked_add(low.checked_shl(shift)?)?;
        if byte & 0x80 == 0 {
            return Some((result as usize, i - offset));
        }
        shift += 7;
        if shift >= 32 {
            return None;
        }
    }
}

```rust
pub(crate) fn collect_coredump_funcs(&self) -> Vec<CompiledCoredumpFunc> {
    let funcs = self.funcs.lock();
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    for (_key, entity) in funcs.iter() {
        if let FuncEntity::Compiled(compiled) = entity {
            if let Some(meta) = compiled.coredump_meta() {
                let ops = compiled.ops();
                let start = ops.as_ptr() as usize;
                let end = start + ops.len();
                result.push(CompiledCoredumpFunc { start, end, meta: meta.clone() });
            }
        }
    }
    result
}
```

use crate::collections::arena::ArenaKey;
use core::{fmt, marker::PhantomData};

/// A handle for a stored owned entity.
pub trait Handle: Copy {
    /// The raw representation of the handle.
    type Raw: ArenaKey;
    /// The store owned entity type of the handle.
    type Entity;
    /// The owner associating reference.
    type Owned<T>;

    /// Returns a shared reference to the raw handle to the store owned entity.
    fn as_raw(&self) -> &Self::Owned<RawHandle<Self>>;

    /// Creates `Self` from its raw representation.
    fn from_raw(raw: Self::Owned<RawHandle<Self>>) -> Self;
}

/// A raw handle with an associated handle type.
pub struct RawHandle<T: Handle> {
    /// The raw underlying handle.
    raw: <T as Handle>::Raw,
    /// Marker to signal the associated handle type.
    marker: PhantomData<T>,
}

impl<T: Handle> RawHandle<T> {
    /// Creates a new [`RawHandle`] from the underlying raw representation.]
    // TODO: this is pub for `Nullable<ExternRef,Func>::from_raw_parts`, not sure if really necessary
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn new(raw: <T as Handle>::Raw) -> Self {
        Self {
            raw,
            marker: PhantomData,
        }
    }

    /// Returns the raw underlying handle value.
    #[inline]
    pub(crate) fn raw(self) -> <T as Handle>::Raw {
        self.raw
    }
}

impl<T: Handle> ArenaKey for RawHandle<T> {
    #[inline]
    fn into_usize(self) -> usize {
        self.raw.into_usize()
    }

    #[inline]
    fn from_usize(value: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        <<T as Handle>::Raw as ArenaKey>::from_usize(value).map(Self::new)
    }
}

impl<T: Handle> Clone for RawHandle<T> {
    #[inline]
    fn clone(&self) -> Self {
        *self
    }
}
impl<T: Handle> Copy for RawHandle<T> {}

impl<T: Handle> PartialEq for RawHandle<T>
where
    T::Raw: PartialEq,
{
    #[inline]
    fn eq(&self, other: &Self) -> bool {
        self.raw == other.raw
    }
}

impl<T: Handle> Eq for RawHandle<T> where T::Raw: Eq {}

impl<T: Handle> PartialOrd for RawHandle<T>
where
    T::Raw: PartialOrd,
{
    #[inline]
    fn partial_cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> Option<core::cmp::Ordering> {
        self.raw.partial_cmp(&other.raw)
    }
}

impl<T: Handle> Ord for RawHandle<T>
where
    T::Raw: Ord,
{
    #[inline]
    fn cmp(&self, other: &Self) -> core::cmp::Ordering {
        self.raw.cmp(&other.raw)
    }
}

impl<T> fmt::Debug for RawHandle<T>
where
    T: Handle<Raw: fmt::Debug>,
{
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.debug_struct("RawHandle")
            .field("key", &self.raw)
            .field("marker", &::core::any::type_name::<T>())
            .finish()
    }
}

/// A unique store identifier.
///
/// # Note
///
/// Used to differentiate different store instances.
#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct StoreId(u32);

impl StoreId {
    /// Returns a new unique [`StoreId`].
    pub(super) fn new() -> Self {
        use core::sync::atomic::{AtomicU32, Ordering};
        /// An atomic, static store identifier counter.
        static STORE_ID: AtomicU32 = AtomicU32::new(0);
        let next = STORE_ID.fetch_add(1, Ordering::AcqRel);
        Self(next)
    }
}

/// A value associated to a [`Store`].
#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Stored<T> {
    /// The identifier of the associated store.
    store: StoreId,
    /// The stored value.
    value: T,
}

/// Trait implemented by utilities that can wrap or unwrap [`Stored`] values.
pub trait AsStoreId: Copy {
    /// Wraps the given `value` as [`Stored<T>`] associating it with `self`.
    fn wrap<T>(self, value: T) -> Stored<T>;

    /// Unwraps the given [`Stored<T>`] reference and returns the `T`.
    ///
    /// Returns `None` if `value` does not originate from `self`.
    fn unwrap<T>(self, value: &Stored<T>) -> Option<&T>;
}

impl AsStoreId for StoreId {
    #[inline]
    fn wrap<T>(self, value: T) -> Stored<T> {
        Stored { store: self, value }
    }

    #[inline]
    fn unwrap<T>(self, value: &Stored<T>) -> Option<&T> {
        if value.store != self {
            return None;
        }
        Some(&value.value)
    }
}

impl AsStoreId for &'_ StoreId {
    #[inline]
    fn wrap<T>(self, value: T) -> Stored<T> {
        <StoreId as AsStoreId>::wrap(*self, value)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn unwrap<T>(self, value: &Stored<T>) -> Option<&T> {
        <StoreId as AsStoreId>::unwrap(*self, value)
    }
}

impl AsStoreId for &'_ StoreInner {
    #[inline]
    fn wrap<T>(self, value: T) -> Stored<T> {
        self.id().wrap(value)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn unwrap<T>(self, value: &Stored<T>) -> Option<&T> {
        self.id().unwrap(value)
    }
}

impl<D> AsStoreId for &'_ Store<D> {
    #[inline]
    fn wrap<T>(self, value: T) -> Stored<T> {
        self.inner.wrap(value)
    }

    #[inline]
    fn unwrap<T>(self, value: &Stored<T>) -> Option<&T> {
        self.inner.unwrap(value)
    }
}

impl AsStoreId for &'_ PrunedStore {
    #[inline]
    fn wrap<T>(self, value: T) -> Stored<T> {
        self.inner().wrap(value)
    }

`unwrap_stored` is pub(super) (private to store module). Coredump module can't use it directly unless we add methods. But we can add a public(crate)
method on StoreInner to get raw index from handle, or iterate handles.

Simpler approach: in coredump, we can iterate over all *instances* and their memories/globals, and assign coredump memory/global indices by identity
(pointer to CoreMemory/CoreGlobal). We don't need store-level iteration if we collect from instances. But host-created memories/globals not referenced
by any instance would be missed. For coredump, including instance-referenced ones is the most important. Host memories/globals passed as imports are
in instances. Standalone host memories/globals aren't part of any module execution and likely not needed. Wasmtime includes them, but for our
purposes, instance-referenced is sufficient.

However, to map a `Memory` handle to a coredump index, I need an identity key. I can use the pointer of the resolved `CoreMemory` entity:
`store.inner().resolve_memory(&mem)` returns `&CoreMemory`, and `as *const CoreMemory as usize` is stable. Same for `Global`. And instance's
memories/globals are handles that resolve to entities. So I can build maps from entity pointer → coredump index by iterating instances. That avoids
needing raw arena keys.

But what about duplicate memories shared between instances? Resolve pointer dedup handles that.

So coredump generation:
1. Iterate all initialized instances via StoreInner accessor `instances()` returning `impl Iterator<Item=&InstanceEntity>`.
2. For each instance, resolve its memories/globals to build memory/global lists (dedup by entity pointer), and record module.
3. Build memory section from the memory list (CoreMemory).
4. Build global section from the global list (CoreGlobal) — only numeric.
5. Build data section from memory list.
6. Build coremodules from dedup modules.
7. Build coreinstances mapping instance entity pointer → index, with module index and memory/global indices.
8. Build corestack from frames.

I need `StoreInner` to expose:
- `instances()` iterator
- `resolve_memory(&Memory) -> &CoreMemory`
- `resolve_global(&Global) -> &CoreGlobal`
- `resolve_instance(&Instance) -> &InstanceEntity` (not needed if iterating)
- `resolve_func` for func index? Not needed since we store func_idx in meta.

Actually `resolve_memory` and `resolve_global` already exist (panicking getters, public on StoreInner). `instances()` we need to add. Also
`InstanceEntity` exposes `memories()` / `globals()` accessors? It has `get_memory(index)`, `get_global(index)` and `exports` but not direct slices.
Let me add `memories()` and `globals()` returning `&[Memory]`/`&[Global]`.

Let me add those to InstanceEntity. And add `StoreInner::instances()`.

Also for the frame's instance → instance index: the frame's `Inst` is a pointer to InstanceEntity. The instances iterator yields `&InstanceEntity`. We
can compare `ptr::eq`. So build `Vec<*const InstanceEntity>` or `Vec<usize>` for coreinstances order. Good.

Frame capture function:
```rust
pub(crate) struct CapturedFrame {
    pub instance_ptr: usize,
    pub func_idx: u32,
    pub locals: Vec<CoredumpValue>,
    pub stack: Vec<CoredumpValue>,
}

pub(crate) fn capture_stack(
    stack: &Stack,
    store: &StoreInner,
    funcs: &[CompiledCoredumpFunc],
) -> Vec<CapturedFrame> {
    let mut frames = Vec::new();
    let cells = stack.cells();
    let callstack_frames = stack.frames();
    let mut cur_instance = stack.current_instance();
    for frame in callstack_frames.iter().rev() {
        let instance = cur_instance;
        // determine meta
        let meta = find_func(funcs, frame.ip_ptr());
        let locals = match &meta {
            Some(m) => read_locals(cells, frame.start_offset(), &m.locals),
            None => Vec::new(),
        };
        let locals_cells = meta.map(|m| locals_cells(&m.locals)).unwrap_or(0);
        let start = frame.start_offset();
        let stack_end = ???; // For top frame, cells.len(); for older frames, next frame's start.
        ...
        frames.push(CapturedFrame { instance_ptr: instance.map(|i| i.raw as usize).unwrap_or(0), func_idx, locals, stack });
        cur_instance = frame.instance_opt().or(cur_instance);
    }
    frames
}
```

Wait, the `stack_end` for each frame: For top frame, end = cells.len(). For older frames, end = next frame's start (the callee frame's start). Since
we iterate from top down, we can track `next_start` (the previously processed frame's start, which is the younger frame's start). For the top frame,
`next_start = cells.len()`. For each subsequent (older) frame, end = current `next_start`, then set `next_start = frame.start_offset()`. So:
```
let mut next_start = cells.len();
for frame in frames.rev() {
    let start = frame.start_offset();
    let stack_values = cells[locals_end..min(next_start, cells.len())] -> Missing values
    ...
    next_start = start;
}
```
But note: for older frames, the callee's start may be greater than `start + locals_cells`; the range is fine. However, is `start + locals_cells`
always <= next_start? For the caller frame, yes: callee.start >= caller.start + caller.locals_cells. For the top frame, start+locals_cells <=
cells.len(). Good. We should clamp.

But wait — the locals values for the *caller* frame after it called a callee: the caller's locals are still intact (locals region is below callee
start). Good.

Now, `find_func`:
```rust
fn find_func(funcs: &[CompiledCoredumpFunc], ip: *const u8) -> Option<&CoredumpFuncMeta> {
    let addr = ip as usize;
    funcs.iter().find(|f| f.start <= addr && addr < f.end).map(|f| &f.meta)
}
```

`read_locals`:
```rust
fn read_locals(cells: &[Cell], start: usize, locals: &[ValType]) -> Vec<CoredumpValue> {
    let mut offset = start;
    let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(locals.len());
    for ty in locals {
        match ty {
            ValType::I32 => { let v = cells.get(offset).map(|c| c.to_bits() as i32).unwrap_or(0); values.push(CoredumpValue::I32(v)); offset += 1; }
            ValType::I64 => ...
            ValType::F32 => { let bits = cells.get(offset).map(|c| c.to_bits() as u32).unwrap_or(0); values.push(CoredumpValue::F32(bits)); offset +=
1; }
            ValType::F64 => ...
            _ => { values.push(CoredumpValue::Missing); offset += cells_for_ty(ty); }
        }
    }
    values
}
```
Wait, for i32 the cell holds the value in low bits as u64 (e.g. -1 stored as u64::from(-1i32 as u32) = 0xFFFFFFFF). `c.to_bits() as i32` gives the
correct i32. For i64, `c.to_bits() as i64`. For f32, `c.to_bits() as u32` gives the f32 bits. For f64, `c.to_bits()`. Good.

But careful: are params/locals stored in cells with the same layout as `RawVal`? Yes, Cell conversion: i32 stores `u64::from(value as u32)`, i64
stores identity, f32 stores `u64::from(f32::to_bits)`, f64 stores `f64::to_bits`. Good.

`locals_cells`:
```rust
fn cells_for_ty(ty: ValType) -> usize { if ty == ValType::V128 { 2 } else { 1 } }
```

Operand stack values: all missing, count = number of cells in range. Each missing = 1 value. `Vec::new()` then extend with Missing for each cell.

Now serialization. Let me define a `Writer` that appends bytes and provides LEB helpers:
```rust
struct Encoder { bytes: Vec<u8> }
impl Encoder {
    fn byte(&mut self, b: u8) { self.bytes.push(b); }
    fn bytes(&mut self, b: &[u8]) { self.bytes.extend_from_slice(b); }
    fn u32(&mut self, v: u32) { // unsigned LEB128 }
    fn u64(&mut self, v: u64) { ... }
    fn i32(&mut self, v: i32) { // signed LEB128 }
    fn i64(&mut self, v: i64) { ... }
    fn name(&mut self, s: &str) { self.u32(s.len() as u32); self.bytes(s.as_bytes()); }
}
```
For f32/f64: `self.bytes(&bits.to_le_bytes())`.

Signed LEB128: standard:
```rust
fn sleb(value: i64) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    let mut more = true;
    let mut v = value;
    while more {
        let mut byte = (v & 0x7f) as u8;
        v >>= 7;
        let sign_bit = byte & 0x40 != 0;
        more = !((v == 0 && !sign_bit) || (v == -1 && sign_bit));
        if more { byte |= 0x80; }
        bytes.push(byte);
    }
    bytes
}
```
For i32, cast to i64 and sleb; the encoding is identical for sign-extended values.

Unsigned LEB128:
```rust
fn uleb(value: u64) -> Vec<u8> {
    let mut bytes = Vec::new();
    let mut v = value;
    loop {
        let mut byte = (v & 0x7f) as u8;
        v >>= 7;
        if v != 0 { byte |= 0x80; }
        bytes.push(byte);
        if v == 0 { break; }
    }
    bytes
}
```

Section writing:
```rust
fn custom_section(enc, name, data) {
    enc.byte(0); // section id
    let size = data.len() + name_len_leb...
```
Actually custom section payload = name (length-prefixed) + data. The section size = LEB size of name length + name bytes + data bytes. We can build
the payload separately then write section with size = payload.len().

Let me write helper:
```rust
fn write_custom_section(out: &mut Vec<u8>, name: &str, data: &[u8]) {
    let mut payload = Vec::new();
    // name: length-prefixed
    push_uleb(&mut payload, name.len() as u64);
    payload.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
    payload.extend_from_slice(data);
    out.push(0);
    push_uleb(out, payload.len() as u64);
    out.extend_from_slice(&payload);
}
```

Standard sections:
```rust
fn write_section(out, id: u8, contents: &[u8]) {
    out.push(id);
    push_uleb(out, contents.len() as u64);
    out.extend_from_slice(contents);
}
```

```rust
pub(crate) fn generate(state: &mut VmState, executable_name: &str) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
```

But `generate` needs `&mut VmState` to access `state.code` (CodeMap, shared) and `state.store` (PrunedStore) and `state.stack`. Actually it only needs
shared access. `state` is `&mut VmState`; we can read fields. `state.code` is `&CodeMap`. `state.store` is `&mut PrunedStore`; we can get
`&StoreInner` via `state.store.inner()`. But careful: if we hold `&StoreInner` and then later access `state.stack` (different field), borrow checker
may complain because `state.store` and `state.stack` are different fields of `state`, but through `&mut state` we can split borrows manually or just
do everything in sequence.

Better design: `generate(store: &StoreInner, code: &CodeMap, stacks: &[&Stack], executable_name)`. The caller in dispatch/mod.rs can split borrows:
```rust
fn handle_trap(state: &mut VmState, trap_code: TrapCode) -> ExecutionOutcome {
    let mut error: Error = trap_code.into();
    if state.store.inner().engine().config().get_generate_coredump() {
        if let Some(coredump) = generate(state) {
            error = error.with_coredump(coredump);
        }
    }
    ExecutionOutcome::from(error)
}
```
where `generate(state)` internally accesses fields sequentially.

Actually, since `VmState` fields are public (`pub store`, `pub stack`, `pub code`), coredump.rs can do:
```rust
pub(crate) fn generate(state: &mut VmState<'_>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {

    // Need &Stack for each. For innermost, use state.stack; for outer, raw ptr.

```
Borrow: `let store = state.store.inner();` borrows state.store immutably. Then `state.code` is a different field, okay if we don't hold `store` across
mutable use of state. `state.stack` is a different field too. But `state.store.inner()` returns `&StoreInner` tied to `&state.store`; then
`state.stack` access is fine because fields are disjoint and Rust allows disjoint field borrows through a `&mut`? Actually `state` is `&mut VmState`,
and accessing `state.store` and `state.stack` and `state.code` as disjoint fields is allowed. But `state.store.inner()` returns `&StoreInner` with
lifetime tied to `&state.store`, which is fine as long as we don't reassign `state.store`. So we can hold `store` and read `state.code` and

However, for the outer stacks (raw pointers), we need `&Stack` from `*mut Stack`. We'll gather raw pointers from thread-local. For the innermost, the
thread-local contains a pointer too, but we'll use `&*state.stack`.

Now, memory/global index mapping:
- `memories: Vec<*const CoreMemory>` in coredump order (dedup). For each instance, resolve each `Memory` handle to `&CoreMemory`, get ptr, find/add to

huge memories this is big but acceptable. Offset 0.

should record the memory's type. Wasmtime uses `mem.ty(&store)` with minimum = current size. In wasmi, `CoreMemory::dynamic_ty()` returns type with

memory section has custom page size flag (bit 0x10?) — but that's a proposal; we'll ignore (assume 64KiB). Most memories are 64KiB.

const expr.

- instance index = index of `instance_ptr` in instances_list.
- func_idx = captured func_idx.
- codeoffset = 0.
- locals count + values.
- stack count + values.

```rust
use core::cell::RefCell;
thread_local! {
    static ACTIVE_STACKS: RefCell<Vec<*mut Stack>> = const { RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };
}
pub(crate) struct ActiveStackGuard {
    stack: *mut Stack,
}
impl ActiveStackGuard {
    pub(crate) fn new(stack: &mut Stack) -> Self {
        let stack = stack as *mut Stack;
        ACTIVE_STACKS.with(|stacks| stacks.borrow_mut().push(stack));
        Self { stack }
    }
}
impl Drop for ActiveStackGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        ACTIVE_STACKS.with(|stacks| {
            let mut stacks = stacks.borrow_mut();
            let popped = stacks.pop();
            debug_assert_eq!(popped, Some(self.stack));
        });
    }
}
fn active_stacks() -> Vec<*mut Stack> {
    ACTIVE_STACKS.with(|stacks| stacks.borrow().clone())
}
```

Now, where to insert the guard in `EngineInner::execute_func` and resumable variants. Let me modify executor/mod.rs.

In `execute_func`:
```rust

let _guard = crate::coredump::ActiveStackGuard::new(&mut stack);
let value = EngineExecutor::new(...)...;
```
But careful: `self.stacks.lock()` returns a guard that holds a MutexGuard; we call `.reuse_or_new()` which returns a Stack. The mutex guard is
temporary and dropped immediately. Then `stack` is local. `ActiveStackGuard::new(&mut stack)` stores raw pointer. Good.

In `execute_func_resumable`:

```rust
let _guard = ActiveStackGuard::new(&mut stack);
let outcome = EngineExecutor::new(...).execute_root_func(...);
```
But after execution, if outcome is Host trap, the stack is moved into `ResumableCallHostTrap` and the guard is dropped (which pops the pointer).
That's fine because the stack is no longer active (suspended). When resumed via `resume_func_host_trap`, we create a new guard.

In `resume_func_host_trap`:
```rust

let _guard = ActiveStackGuard::new(invocation.common.stack_mut());

```
Wait, `stack_mut()` returns `&mut Stack`; but we also pass it to EngineExecutor::new. We need `&mut` for guard creation. Let's see:
`invocation.common.stack_mut()` returns `&mut Stack`; we can create guard from that. But then `executor` holds another `&mut Stack` (same), which
would conflict if we hold both. `EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, invocation.common.stack_mut())` takes `&mut Stack` and stores it; then calling
`stack_mut()` again for guard would be a second mutable borrow → compile error. So we need to create the guard before creating the executor, or get
the pointer once:
```rust
let stack = invocation.common.stack_mut();
let _guard = ActiveStackGuard::new(stack);
let mut executor = EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, stack);
```
But `stack` is `&mut Stack`; passing to both guard and executor moves the `&mut`? `ActiveStackGuard::new(stack)` takes `&mut Stack` by value
(reborrow). If `new` takes `stack: &mut Stack`, it reborrows. Then `EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, stack)` takes `&mut Stack`. After the guard
creation, the reborrow ends, and we can pass `stack` again. Should work if we structure carefully.

Actually `ActiveStackGuard::new(&mut *stack)` to reborrow. Let me make `new` accept `&mut Stack`. Then:
```rust
let stack = invocation.common.stack_mut();
let _guard = ActiveStackGuard::new(stack);
let mut executor = EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, stack);
```
The compiler may complain about `stack` being moved/borrowed. `new(stack)` reborrows `*stack` for the duration of the call (since parameter is `&mut
Stack`), then releases. Then `EngineExecutor::new(..., stack)` reborrows again. Fine.

Similarly for `resume_func_out_of_fuel`.

Also `execute_func` and `execute_func_resumable` already use `&mut stack`.

Now, let me also think about nested `execute_func` inside host functions. The host function is called from `call_host_func` in PrunedStore, which is
called from within `execute_root_func` of the outer execution. The outer guard is still active (it's a local in `EngineInner::execute_func` which is
on the native call stack). When the host calls `func.call(&mut store, ...)`, that calls `EngineInner::execute_func` again → pushes inner guard. Good.

cd /app && cat > crates/wasmi/src/coredump.rs <<'EOF'
//! Wasm coredump generation.
//!
//! This module implements generation of [Wasm coredumps] upon Wasm traps.
//! Coredumps are only generated if this feature is enabled via
//! [`Config::generate_coredump`](crate::Config::generate_coredump).
//!
//! [Wasm coredumps]: https://github.com/WebAssembly/tool-conventions/blob/main/Coredump.md

use crate::{
    Global,
    InstanceEntity,
    Memory,
    ValType,
    core::{CoreGlobal, CoreMemory},
    engine::{
        CompiledCoredumpFunc,
        CoredumpFuncMeta,
        Stack,
        executor::handler::state::VmState,
    },
    store::StoreInner,
};
use alloc::{boxed::Box, string::String, vec, vec::Vec};
use core::cell::RefCell;

/// A stack frame captured for a Wasm coredump.
pub(crate) struct CapturedFrame {
    /// The pointer of the [`InstanceEntity`] of the frame.
    pub instance_ptr: usize,
    /// The Wasm function index of the frame within its module.
    pub func_idx: u32,
    /// The local values of the frame.
    pub locals: Vec<CoredumpValue>,
    /// The operand stack values of the frame.
    pub stack: Vec<CoredumpValue>,
}

/// A single value captured for a Wasm coredump.
#[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone)]
pub(crate) enum CoredumpValue {
    /// A value that could not be recovered.
    Missing,
    /// An `i32` value.
    I32(i32),
    /// An `i64` value.
    I64(i64),
    /// An `f32` value encoded as its IEEE 754 bits.
    F32(u32),
    /// An `f64` value encoded as its IEEE 754 bits.
    F64(u64),
}

/// A guard registering a [`Stack`] as currently active.
///
/// # Note
///
/// This is required to correctly generate Wasm coredumps for re-entrant
/// Wasm executions where multiple [`Stack`]s may be active at the same time.
pub(crate) struct ActiveStackGuard {
    stack: *mut Stack,
}

impl ActiveStackGuard {
    /// Creates a new [`ActiveStackGuard`] for the given [`Stack`].
    pub(crate) fn new(stack: &mut Stack) -> Self {
        let stack = stack as *mut Stack;
        ACTIVE_STACKS.with(|stacks| stacks.borrow_mut().push(stack));
        Self { stack }
    }
}

impl Drop for ActiveStackGuard {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        ACTIVE_STACKS.with(|stacks| {
            let mut stacks = stacks.borrow_mut();
            let popped = stacks.pop();
            debug_assert_eq!(popped, Some(self.stack));
        });
    }
}

thread_local! {
    /// The stacks of all currently active Wasm executions on this thread.
    ///
    /// # Note
    ///
    /// The stacks are stored in order from outermost to innermost execution.
    static ACTIVE_STACKS: RefCell<Vec<*mut Stack>> = const { RefCell::new(Vec::new()) };
}

/// Returns the [`Stack`]s of all currently active Wasm executions.
///
/// # Note
///
/// The returned stacks are ordered from outermost to innermost execution.
fn active_stacks() -> Vec<*mut Stack> {
    ACTIVE_STACKS.with(|stacks| stacks.borrow().clone())
}

/// Generates a Wasm coredump for the currently active execution.
///
/// Returns `None` if coredump generation is not possible.
pub(crate) fn generate(state: &mut VmState<'_>) -> Option<Vec<u8>> {
    let store = state.store.inner();
    let code = state.code;
    let executable_name = store.engine().config().get_coredump_executable_name().to_owned();
    let funcs = code.collect_coredump_funcs();

    // Capture frames from all active stacks, innermost first.
    let stack_pointers = active_stacks();
    let mut frames = Vec::new();
    for stack_ptr in stack_pointers.iter().rev() {
        // Safety: the active stacks are alive for the entire duration of the
        // innermost execution and never mutated while we generate the coredump.
        let stack = unsafe { &**stack_ptr };
        let mut captured = capture_stack(stack, store, &funcs);
        frames.append(&mut captured);
    }

    // Collect modules, instances, memories and globals from the store.
    let mut modules: Vec<ModuleInfo> = Vec::new();
    let mut instances: Vec<&InstanceEntity> = Vec::new();
    let mut memories: Vec<*const CoreMemory> = Vec::new();
    let mut globals: Vec<*const CoreGlobal> = Vec::new();

    for instance in store.instances() {
        if !instance.is_initialized() {
            continue;
        }
        // Add module.
        if let Some(module) = instance.module() {
            let id = module.unique_id();
            if !modules.iter().any(|m| m.id == id) {
                let name = module
                    .name()
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("module-{}", modules.len()));
                modules.push(ModuleInfo { id, name });
            }
        }
        // Add memories and globals.
        for memory in instance.memories() {
            let core = store.resolve_memory(memory);
            let ptr = core as *const CoreMemory;
            if !memories.contains(&ptr) {
                memories.push(ptr);
            }
        }
        for global in instance.globals() {
            let core = store.resolve_global(global);
            if !core.ty().content().is_num() {
                continue;
            }
            let ptr = core as *const CoreGlobal;
            if !globals.contains(&ptr) {
                globals.push(ptr);
            }
        }
        instances.push(instance);
    }

    // Build maps from entity pointer to coredump index.
    let module_index = |instance: &InstanceEntity| -> u32 {
        let Some(module) = instance.module() else {
            return 0;
        };
        let id = module.unique_id();
        modules
            .iter()
            .position(|m| m.id == id)
            .unwrap_or(0) as u32
    };
    let memory_index = |memory: &Memory| -> u32 {
        let core = store.resolve_memory(memory);
        let ptr = core as *const CoreMemory;
        memories
            .iter()
            .position(|m| *m == ptr)
            .unwrap_or(u32::MAX as usize) as u32
    };
    let global_index = |global: &Global| -> Option<u32> {
        let core = store.resolve_global(global);
        if !core.ty().content().is_num() {
            return None;
        }
        let ptr = core as *const CoreGlobal;
        Some(globals.iter().position(|g| *g == ptr).unwrap_or(u32::MAX as usize) as u32)
    };
    let instance_index = |ptr: usize| -> u32 {
        instances
            .iter()
            .position(|i| i as *const InstanceEntity as usize == ptr)
            .unwrap_or(u32::MAX as usize) as u32
    };

    let mut out = Vec::new();

    // 1. "core" custom section.
    let mut core_data = Vec::new();
    core_data.push(0x00);
    push_name(&mut core_data, &executable_name);
    write_custom_section(&mut out, "core", &core_data);

    // 2. Memory section.
    let mut memory_contents = Vec::new();
    {
        let mut contents = Vec::new();
        push_uleb(&mut contents, memories.len() as u64);
        for &memory_ptr in &memories {
            // Safety: all memory pointers refer to live entities in the store.
            let memory = unsafe { &*memory_ptr };
            let ty = memory.dynamic_ty();
            let minimum = ty.minimum();
            let maximum = ty.maximum();
            let mut flags = 0u64;
            if maximum.is_some() {
                flags |= 0x01;
            }
            if ty.is_64() {
                flags |= 0x04;
            }
            push_uleb(&mut contents, flags);
            push_uleb(&mut contents, minimum);
            if let Some(maximum) = maximum {
                push_uleb(&mut contents, maximum);
            }
        }
        write_section(&mut out, 5, &contents);
    }

    // 3. Global section.
    {
        let mut contents = Vec::new();
        push_uleb(&mut contents, globals.len() as u64);
        for &global_ptr in &globals {
            // Safety: all global pointers refer to live entities in the store.
            let global = unsafe { &*global_ptr };
            let ty = global.ty();
            push_val_type(&mut contents, ty.content());
            contents.push(match ty.mutability() {
                crate::core::Mutability::Const => 0x00,
                crate::core::Mutability::Var => 0x01,
            });
            let value = global.get();
            write_const_expr(&mut contents, ty.content(), value.raw().to_bits64());
        }
        write_section(&mut out, 6, &contents);
    }

    // 4. Data section.
    {
        let mut contents = Vec::new();
        push_uleb(&mut contents, memories.len() as u64);
        for (idx, &memory_ptr) in memories.iter().enumerate() {
            // Safety: all memory pointers refer to live entities in the store.
            let memory = unsafe { &*memory_ptr };
            let data = memory.data();
            if idx == 0 {
                contents.push(0x00);
            } else {
                contents.push(0x02);
                push_uleb(&mut contents, idx as u64);
            }
            // i32.const offset 0, end
            contents.push(0x41);
            push_uleb(&mut contents, 0);
            contents.push(0x0B);
            push_uleb(&mut contents, data.len() as u64);
            contents.extend_from_slice(data);
        }
        write_section(&mut out, 11, &contents);
    }

    // 5. "coremodules" custom section.
    let mut modules_data = Vec::new();
    push_uleb(&mut modules_data, modules.len() as u64);
    for module in &modules {
        modules_data.push(0x00);
        push_name(&mut modules_data, &module.name);
    }
    write_custom_section(&mut out, "coremodules", &modules_data);

    // 6. "coreinstances" custom section.
    let mut instances_data = Vec::new();
    push_uleb(&mut instances_data, instances.len() as u64);
    for instance in &instances {
        instances_data.push(0x00);
        push_uleb(&mut instances_data, module_index(instance) as u64);
        let memories = instance
            .memories()
            .iter()
            .map(memory_index)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        push_uleb(&mut instances_data, memories.len() as u64);
        for memory in memories {
            push_uleb(&mut instances_data, memory as u64);
        }
        let globals = instance
            .globals()
            .iter()
            .filter_map(global_index)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        push_uleb(&mut instances_data, globals.len() as u64);
        for global in globals {
            push_uleb(&mut instances_data, global as u64);
        }
    }
    write_custom_section(&mut out, "coreinstances", &instances_data);

    // 7. "corestack" custom section.
    let mut stack_data = Vec::new();
    stack_data.push(0x00);
    push_name(&mut stack_data, "main");
    push_uleb(&mut stack_data, frames.len() as u64);
    for frame in &frames {
        stack_data.push(0x00);
        push_uleb(&mut stack_data, instance_index(frame.instance_ptr) as u64);
        push_uleb(&mut stack_data, frame.func_idx as u64);
        // Note: Wasmi does not retain enough information to recover the
        //       exact Wasm code offset of the frame.
        push_uleb(&mut stack_data, 0);
        push_uleb(&mut stack_data, frame.locals.len() as u64);
        for value in &frame.locals {
            write_value(&mut stack_data, *value);
        }
        push_uleb(&mut stack_data, frame.stack.len() as u64);
        for value in &frame.stack {
            write_value(&mut stack_data, *value);
        }
    }
    write_custom_section(&mut out, "corestack", &stack_data);

    // Prepend the Wasm header.
    let mut result = Vec::with_capacity(out.len() + 8);
    result.extend_from_slice(b"\0asm");
    result.extend_from_slice(&1u32.to_le_bytes());
    result.extend_from_slice(&out);
    Some(result)
}

/// Information about a module in the coredump.
struct ModuleInfo {
    /// A unique identifier of the module.
    id: *const (),
    /// The name of the module.
    name: String,
}

/// Captures the stack frames of the given [`Stack`].
fn capture_stack(
    stack: &Stack,
    _store: &StoreInner,
    funcs: &[CompiledCoredumpFunc],
) -> Vec<CapturedFrame> {
    let cells = stack.cells();
    let frames = stack.frames();
    let mut result = Vec::new();
    let mut next_start = cells.len();
    let mut cur_instance = stack.current_instance();

    for frame in frames.iter().rev() {
        let start = frame.start_offset();
        let meta = find_func(funcs, frame.ip_ptr());
        let (locals, locals_cells) = match meta {
            Some(meta) => (read_locals(cells, start, &meta.locals), locals_cells(&meta.locals)),
            None => (Vec::new(), 0),
        };
        let locals_end = start.saturating_add(locals_cells);
        let stack_end = next_start.min(cells.len());
        let stack_len = stack_end.saturating_sub(locals_end);
        let stack = (0..stack_len)
            .map(|_| CoredumpValue::Missing)
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let instance_ptr = cur_instance
            .map(|inst| inst.as_ptr() as usize)
            .unwrap_or(0);
        result.push(CapturedFrame {
            instance_ptr,
            func_idx: meta.map(|m| m.func_idx).unwrap_or(0),
            locals,
            stack,
        });
        next_start = start;
        // Move to the caller instance.
        if let Some(prev) = frame.instance_opt() {
            cur_instance = Some(prev);
        }
    }
    result
}

/// Finds the coredump metadata of the compiled function containing `ip`.
fn find_func(funcs: &[CompiledCoredumpFunc], ip: *const u8) -> Option<&CoredumpFuncMeta> {
    let addr = ip as usize;
    funcs
        .iter()
        .find(|func| func.start <= addr && addr < func.end)
        .map(|func| &func.meta)
}

/// Returns the number of cells required to store a value of the given type.
fn cells_for_ty(ty: ValType) -> usize {
    if ty == ValType::V128 {
        2
    } else {
        1
    }
}

/// Returns the total number of cells required to store the given local types.
fn locals_cells(locals: &[ValType]) -> usize {
    locals.iter().copied().map(cells_for_ty).sum()
}

/// Reads the local values of a frame from the value stack.
fn read_locals(cells: &[crate::engine::Cell], start: usize, locals: &[ValType]) -> Vec<CoredumpValue> {
    let mut offset = start;
    let mut values = Vec::with_capacity(locals.len());
    for ty in locals {
        let value = match ty {
            ValType::I32 => cells
                .get(offset)
                .map(|cell| CoredumpValue::I32(cell.to_bits() as i32))
                .unwrap_or(CoredumpValue::Missing),
            ValType::I64 => cells
                .get(offset)
                .map(|cell| CoredumpValue::I64(cell.to_bits() as i64))
                .unwrap_or(CoredumpValue::Missing),
            ValType::F32 => cells
                .get(offset)
                .map(|cell| CoredumpValue::F32(cell.to_bits() as u32))
                .unwrap_or(CoredumpValue::Missing),
            ValType::F64 => cells
                .get(offset)
                .map(|cell| CoredumpValue::F64(cell.to_bits()))
                .unwrap_or(CoredumpValue::Missing),
            _ => CoredumpValue::Missing,
        };
        values.push(value);
        offset = offset.saturating_add(cells_for_ty(*ty));
    }
    values
}

/// Writes an unsigned LEB128 encoded `u64` to `out`.
fn push_uleb(out: &mut Vec<u8>, mut value: u64) {
    loop {
        let mut byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;
        value >>= 7;
        if value != 0 {
            byte |= 0x80;
        }
        out.push(byte);
        if value == 0 {
            break;
        }
    }
}

/// Writes a signed LEB128 encoded `i64` to `out`.
fn push_sleb(out: &mut Vec<u8>, value: i64) {
    let mut value = value;
    loop {
        let mut byte = (value & 0x7f) as u8;
        value >>= 7;
        let sign_bit_set = byte & 0x40 != 0;
        let done = (value == 0 && !sign_bit_set) || (value == -1 && sign_bit_set);
        if !done {
            byte |= 0x80;
        }
        out.push(byte);
        if done {
            break;
        }
    }
}

/// Writes a name (LEB128 length-prefixed UTF-8 string) to `out`.
fn push_name(out: &mut Vec<u8>, name: &str) {
    push_uleb(out, name.len() as u64);
    out.extend_from_slice(name.as_bytes());
}

/// Writes a Wasm value type byte to `out`.
fn push_val_type(out: &mut Vec<u8>, ty: ValType) {
    let byte = match ty {
        ValType::I32 => 0x7F,
        ValType::I64 => 0x7E,
        ValType::F32 => 0x7D,
        ValType::F64 => 0x7C,
        ValType::V128 => 0x7B,
        ValType::FuncRef => 0x70,
        ValType::ExternRef => 0x6F,
    };
    out.push(byte);
}

/// Writes a constant expression for the given numeric `value` of type `ty`.
fn write_const_expr(out: &mut Vec<u8>, ty: ValType, bits: u64) {
    match ty {
        ValType::I32 => {
            out.push(0x41);
            push_sleb(out, bits as u32 as i32 as i64);
        }
        ValType::I64 => {
            out.push(0x42);
            push_sleb(out, bits as i64);
        }
        ValType::F32 => {
            out.push(0x43);
            out.extend_from_slice(&(bits as u32).to_le_bytes());
        }
        ValType::F64 => {
            out.push(0x44);
            out.extend_from_slice(&bits.to_le_bytes());
        }
        // Note: non-numeric globals are not included in coredumps.
        _ => unreachable!("non-numeric global value in coredump"),
    }
    out.push(0x0B);
}

/// Writes a [`CoredumpValue`] to `out`.
fn write_value(out: &mut Vec<u8>, value: CoredumpValue) {
    match value {
        CoredumpValue::Missing => out.push(0x01),
        CoredumpValue::I32(value) => {
            out.push(0x7F);
            push_sleb(out, value as i64);
        }
        CoredumpValue::I64(value) => {
            out.push(0x7E);
            push_sleb(out, value);
        }
        CoredumpValue::F32(bits) => {
            out.push(0x7D);
            out.extend_from_slice(&bits.to_le_bytes());
        }
        CoredumpValue::F64(bits) => {
            out.push(0x7C);
            out.extend_from_slice(&bits.to_le_bytes());
        }
    }
}

/// Writes a custom section with the given `name` and `data` to `out`.
fn write_custom_section(out: &mut Vec<u8>, name: &str, data: &[u8]) {
    let mut payload = Vec::new();
    push_name(&mut payload, name);
    payload.extend_from_slice(data);
    out.push(0x00);
    push_uleb(out, payload.len() as u64);
    out.extend_from_slice(&payload);
}

/// Writes a standard Wasm section with the given `id` and `contents` to `out`.
fn write_section(out: &mut Vec<u8>, id: u8, contents: &[u8]) {
    out.push(id);
    push_uleb(out, contents.len() as u64);
    out.extend_from_slice(contents);
}

            .map_err(ExecutionOutcome::into_non_resumable)?;
        self.stacks.lock().recycle(stack);
        Ok(value)
    }

    /// Executes the given [`Func`] resumably with the given `params` and returns the `results`.
    ///
    /// Uses the [`StoreContextMut`] for context information about the Wasm [`Store`].
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// If the Wasm execution traps or runs out of resources.
    pub fn execute_func_resumable<T, Params, Results>(
        &self,
        ctx: StoreContextMut<T>,
        func: &Func,
        params: Params,
        results: Results,
    ) -> Result<ResumableCallBase<Results::Value>, Error>
    where
        Params: LowerToCells,
        Results: LiftFromCells,
    {
        let store = ctx.store;
        let mut stack = self.stacks.lock().reuse_or_new();
        let outcome = EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, &mut stack)
            .execute_root_func(store, func, params, results);
        let value = match outcome {
            Ok(value) => value,
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::Host(error)) => {
                let host_func = *error.host_func();
                let caller_results = *error.caller_results();
                let host_error = error.into_error();
                return Ok(ResumableCallBase::HostTrap(ResumableCallHostTrap::new(
                    store.engine().clone(),
                    stack,
                    *func,
                    host_func,
                    host_error,
                    caller_results,
                )));
            }
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::OutOfFuel(error)) => {
                let required_fuel = error.required_fuel();
                return Ok(ResumableCallBase::OutOfFuel(ResumableCallOutOfFuel::new(
                    store.engine().clone(),
                    stack,
                    *func,
                    required_fuel,
                )));
            }
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::Error(error)) => {
                self.stacks.lock().recycle(stack);
                return Err(error);
            }
        };
        self.stacks.lock().recycle(stack);
    ///
    /// Uses the [`StoreContextMut`] for context information about the Wasm [`Store`].
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// If the Wasm execution traps or runs out of resources.
    pub fn resume_func_host_trap<T, Params, Results>(
        &self,
        ctx: StoreContextMut<T>,
        mut invocation: ResumableCallHostTrap,
        params: Params,
        results: Results,
    ) -> Result<ResumableCallBase<Results::Value>, Error>
    where
        Params: LowerToCells,
        Results: LiftFromCells,
    {
        let caller_results = invocation.caller_results();
        let mut executor = EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, invocation.common.stack_mut());
        let outcome = executor.resume_func_host_trap(ctx.store, params, caller_results, results);
        let results = match outcome {
            Ok(results) => results,
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::Host(error)) => {
                let host_func = *error.host_func();
                let caller_results = *error.caller_results();
                invocation.update(host_func, error.into_error(), caller_results);
                return Ok(ResumableCallBase::HostTrap(invocation));
            }
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::OutOfFuel(error)) => {
                let required_fuel = error.required_fuel();
                let invocation = invocation.update_to_out_of_fuel(required_fuel);
                return Ok(ResumableCallBase::OutOfFuel(invocation));
            }
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::Error(error)) => {
                self.stacks.lock().recycle(invocation.common.take_stack());
                return Err(error);
            }
        };
        self.stacks.lock().recycle(invocation.common.take_stack());
        Ok(ResumableCallBase::Finished(results))
    }

    /// Resumes the given [`Func`] after running out of fuel and returns the `results`.
    ///
    /// Uses the [`StoreContextMut`] for context information about the Wasm [`Store`].
    ///
    /// # Errors
    ///
    /// If the Wasm execution traps or runs out of resources.
    pub fn resume_func_out_of_fuel<T, Results>(
        &self,
        ctx: StoreContextMut<T>,
        mut invocation: ResumableCallOutOfFuel,
        results: Results,
    ) -> Result<ResumableCallBase<Results::Value>, Error>
    where
        Results: LiftFromCells,
    {
        let mut executor = EngineExecutor::new(&self.code_map, invocation.common.stack_mut());
        let outcome = executor.resume_func_out_of_fuel(ctx.store, results);
        let results = match outcome {
            Ok(results) => results,
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::Host(error)) => {
                let host_func = *error.host_func();
                let caller_results = *error.caller_results();
                let invocation =
                    invocation.update_to_host_trap(host_func, error.into_error(), caller_results);
                return Ok(ResumableCallBase::HostTrap(invocation));
            }
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::OutOfFuel(error)) => {
                invocation.update(error.required_fuel());
                return Ok(ResumableCallBase::OutOfFuel(invocation));
            }
            Err(ExecutionOutcome::Error(error)) => {
                self.stacks.lock().recycle(invocation.common.take_stack());
                return Err(error);
            }
        };
        self.stacks.lock().recycle(invocation.common.take_stack());
        Ok(ResumableCallBase::Finished(results))
    }

which contains `store: &mut Store<T>`. We have access to `ctx.store.inner` (StoreInner). But `ActiveStackGuard` currently only takes `&mut Stack`.
We'd need to pass `&StoreInner` too. That's doable: `ActiveStackGuard::new(&mut stack, ctx.store.inner_mut())` or similar.

Actually StoreInner is accessed via `ctx.store` which is `&mut Store<T>`; `ctx.store.inner` is a pub(crate) field (`pub(crate) inner: StoreInner`). So
we can call `ctx.store.inner.push_active_stack(stack_ptr)`.

But in `resume_func_host_trap`, `ctx` is `StoreContextMut<T>` with `ctx.store`. Good.

Let's redesign with StoreInner-based active stack tracking. This avoids thread_local and is no_std friendly. But note: `StoreInner` may be accessed by
multiple threads? A Store is not Sync, so single-threaded. Active stacks within one store are per-thread anyway (host functions are synchronous).
Good.

However, `StoreInner` currently doesn't have a `Stack` import; adding `Vec<*mut Stack>` makes StoreInner contain raw pointers. That's fine (like
EngineStacks). But `StoreInner` is `Debug`; `*mut Stack` implements Debug? Raw pointers implement Debug. Vec<*mut Stack> Debug works.

Let me implement:
- StoreInner field `active_stacks: Vec<*mut Stack>`.
- Methods:
```rust
pub(crate) fn push_active_stack(&mut self, stack: *mut Stack) { self.active_stacks.push(stack); }
pub(crate) fn pop_active_stack(&mut self, expected: *mut Stack) { let popped = self.active_stacks.pop(); debug_assert_eq!(popped, Some(expected)); }
pub(crate) fn active_stacks(&self) -> &[*mut Stack] { &self.active_stacks }
```
- ActiveStackGuard::new(stack: &mut Stack, store: &mut StoreInner) { store.push_active_stack(stack as *mut _); ... }
- Drop: store not available; instead make guard store `store: *mut StoreInner` and on drop call pop. But we'd have a raw pointer to StoreInner. Or
simpler: don't use a guard; push at start and pop at end manually in each execution function. But there are early returns (errors). A guard is
cleaner. The guard can hold `store_ptr: *mut StoreInner` and `stack_ptr`. On drop, `unsafe { &mut *store_ptr }.pop_active_stack(...)`. Since
StoreInner is alive (the execution context holds it), this is fine, similar to existing raw pointer usage.

Actually, can we avoid raw pointers to StoreInner by having the guard hold the `&mut StoreInner`? A guard struct with `store: &'a mut StoreInner` and
Drop impl cannot access `&mut` in Drop (you can't move out). But `Drop` gets `&mut self`, and `self.store` is a `&'a mut StoreInner`; calling methods
on it is allowed in Drop? `Drop::drop(&mut self)` can use `self.store` (it's a field, and `&mut self` allows reborrowing). Actually a struct
containing `&'a mut T` can be dropped; in `drop(&mut self)`, you can call `self.store.pop()` because `&mut self` gives access to the field. Let me
try:
```rust
pub(crate) struct ActiveStackGuard<'a> {
    stack: *mut Stack,
    store: &'a mut StoreInner,
}
impl Drop for ActiveStackGuard<'_> {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        self.store.pop_active_stack(self.stack);
    }
}
```
But this would keep a mutable borrow of StoreInner for the entire execution, which conflicts with
`EngineExecutor::new(...).execute_root_func(ctx.store, ...)` needing `&mut Store<T>`. Because `ctx.store` is `&mut Store<T>`, and StoreInner is a
field of Store; if we hold `&mut StoreInner`, we can't also pass `ctx.store` (which borrows the whole Store). So a borrow of StoreInner can't be held
across execution. Hence raw pointer to StoreInner is needed.

So guard holds raw pointers to both stack and store inner. On drop, deref store pointer. This is acceptable.

Let me implement:
```rust
pub(crate) struct ActiveStackGuard {
    stack: *mut Stack,
    store: *mut StoreInner,
}
impl ActiveStackGuard {
    pub(crate) fn new(stack: &mut Stack, store: &mut StoreInner) -> Self {
        let stack_ptr = stack as *mut Stack;
        let store_ptr = store as *mut StoreInner;
        // Safety: store is alive for the duration of the guard.
        unsafe { (&mut *store_ptr).push_active_stack(stack_ptr) };
        Self { stack: stack_ptr, store: store_ptr }
    }
}
impl Drop ... { unsafe { (&mut *self.store).pop_active_stack(self.stack) } }
```

Then `generate(state)` uses `store.active_stacks()` (slice of `*mut Stack`) instead of thread_local.

Let's update StoreInner, coredump.rs, and executor/mod.rs call sites to pass `&mut StoreInner`.

In `execute_func`:


Borrow ends after guard creation (guard only stores raw pointer). Should be fine.

In `execute_func_resumable`: `let store = ctx.store;` then `&mut store.inner`.

In resume functions: `ctx.store.inner`.

/// A trait used to get shared access to a [`Store`] in Wasmi.

    /// The user state associated with the [`Store`], aka the `T` in `Store<T>`.

impl<I> ops::Index<I> for SmallByteSlice
where
    I: slice::SliceIndex<[u8]>,
{
    type Output = <I as slice::SliceIndex<[u8]>>::Output;

    #[inline]
    fn index(&self, index: I) -> &Self::Output {
        self.as_slice().index(index)
    }
}

impl<'a> From<&'a [u8]> for SmallByteSlice {
    fn from(bytes: &'a [u8]) -> Self {
        if bytes.len() <= Self::MAX_INLINE_SIZE {
            let len = bytes.len() as u8;
            let mut buffer = [0x00_u8; Self::MAX_INLINE_SIZE];
            buffer[..usize::from(len)].copy_from_slice(bytes);
            return Self::Small { len, bytes: buffer };
        }
        Self::Big(bytes.into())
    }
}

/// Meta information about a [`EngineFunc`].
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct CompiledFuncEntity {
    /// The sequence of [`Op`] of the [`CompiledFuncEntity`].
    ops: Pin<Box<[u8]>>,
    /// The number of stack slots used by the [`EngineFunc`] in total.
    ///
    /// # Note
    ///
    /// This includes stack slots to store the function local constant values,
    /// function parameters, function locals and dynamically used stack slots.
    len_stack_slots: u16,
}

impl CompiledFuncEntity {
    /// Returns the sequence of encoded [`Op`]s of the [`CompiledFuncEntity`].
    pub(crate) fn ops(&self) -> &[u8] {
        self.ops.as_ref()
    }

    /// Returns the coredump metadata of the [`CompiledFuncEntity`] if any.
    pub(crate) fn coredump_meta(&self) -> Option<&CoredumpFuncMeta> {
        self.coredump.as_ref()
    }

    /// Create a new initialized [`CompiledFuncEntity`].
    ///
    /// # Panics
    ///
    /// - If `ops` is empty.
    /// - If `ops` contains more than `i32::MAX` encoded bytes.
    pub fn new(len_stack_slots: u16, ops: &[u8], coredump: Option<CoredumpFuncMeta>) -> Self {
        let ops: Pin<Box<[u8]>> = Pin::new(ops.into());
        assert!(
            !ops.is_empty(),
            "compiled functions must have at least one instruction"
        );
        assert!(
            // Generally, Wasmi has no issues with more than `i32::MAX` instructions.
            // However, Wasmi's branch instructions can jump across at most `i32::MAX`
            // forwards or `i32::MIN` instructions backwards and thus having more than
            // `i32::MAX` instructions might introduce problems.
            ops.len() <= i32::MAX as usize,
            "compiled function has too many instructions: {}",
            ops.len(),
        );
        Self {
            ops,
            len_stack_slots,
            coredump,
        }
    }
}

But there's a subtlety: the trap function's locals — does `unreachable` trap at a point where locals are initialized? Yes, local.get writes them. We
need a function:
```wat
(func (export "trap") (param i32) (param i64) (param f32) (param f64) (local i32)
    local.get 0
    local.get 1
    local.get 2
    local.get 3
    local.get 4
    drop drop drop drop drop
    unreachable
)
```
Actually `drop` consumes them; simpler just to have `unreachable` after locals are set. Locals are initialized to 0 by default; params get values. We
can just `unreachable` and params will have the passed values. Let's use params i32=42, i64=-7, f32=1.5, f64=-2.25, and a local i32 set to 99 via
local.set before unreachable.

`.name()` and `.data()`. For memory/global/data: `Payload::MemorySection(reader)`, etc.

use wasmi::{Config, Engine, Linker, Module, Store};
use wasmparser::{Parser, Payload, CoreDumpStackSection, CoreDumpInstancesSection, CoreDumpModulesSection, CoreDumpSection};

#[test]
fn coredump_sections_and_frames() {
    let mut config = Config::default();
    config.generate_coredump(true);
    config.coredump_executable_name("myexe");
    let engine = Engine::new(&config);
    let module = Module::new(
        &engine,
        r#"
        (module
            (memory (export "mem") 1)
            (global (export "g") i32 (i32.const 7))
            (func (export "trap") (param i32) (param i64) (param f32) (param f64) (local i32)
                local.get 0
                drop
                local.get 1
                drop
                local.get 2
                drop
                local.get 3
                drop
                i32.const 99
                local.set 4
                unreachable
            )
        )
        "#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());
    let linker = Linker::new(&engine);
    let instance = linker.instantiate_and_start(&mut store, &module).unwrap();
    let func = instance.get_typed_func::<(i32, i64, f32, f64), ()>(&store, "trap").unwrap();
    let error = func.call(&mut store, (42, -7, 1.5f32, -2.25f64)).unwrap_err();
    let coredump = error.coredump().expect("coredump should be present");
    std::fs::write("/tmp/coredump.wasm", coredump).unwrap();

    let mut saw_core = false;
    let mut saw_modules = false;
    let mut saw_instances = false;
    let mut saw_stack = false;
    let mut saw_memory = false;
    let mut saw_global = false;
    let mut saw_data = false;

    for payload in Parser::new(0).parse_all(coredump) {
        let payload = payload.unwrap();
        match payload {
            Payload::CustomSection(reader) => match reader.name() {
                "core" => {
                    saw_core = true;
                    let data = reader.data();
                    let sec = CoreDumpSection::new(wasmparser::BinaryReader::new(data, 0)).unwrap();
                    assert_eq!(sec.name, "myexe");
                }
                "coremodules" => {
                    saw_modules = true;
                    let data = reader.data();
                    let sec = CoreDumpModulesSection::new(wasmparser::BinaryReader::new(data, 0)).unwrap();
                    eprintln!("modules: {:?}", sec.modules);
                }
                "coreinstances" => {
                    saw_instances = true;
                    let data = reader.data();
                    let sec = CoreDumpInstancesSection::new(wasmparser::BinaryReader::new(data, 0)).unwrap();
                    eprintln!("instances: {:?}", sec.instances);
                }
                "corestack" => {
                    saw_stack = true;
                    let data = reader.data();
                    let sec = CoreDumpStackSection::new(wasmparser::BinaryReader::new(data, 0)).unwrap();
                    eprintln!("name: {:?} frames: {}", sec.name, sec.frames.len());
                    assert_eq!(sec.name, "main");
                    assert_eq!(sec.frames.len(), 1);
                    let frame = &sec.frames[0];
                    assert_eq!(frame.funcidx, 0);
                    assert_eq!(frame.codeoffset, 0);
                    eprintln!("locals: {:?}", frame.locals);
                    assert_eq!(frame.locals.len(), 5);
                    match frame.locals[0] { wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::I32(v) => assert_eq!(v, 42), _ => panic!() }
                    match frame.locals[1] { wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::I64(v) => assert_eq!(v, -7), _ => panic!() }
                    match frame.locals[2] { wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::F32(v) => assert_eq!(v, 1.5), _ => panic!() }
                    match frame.locals[3] { wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::F64(v) => assert_eq!(v, -2.25), _ => panic!() }
                    match frame.locals[4] { wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::I32(v) => assert_eq!(v, 99), _ => panic!() }
                }
                _ => {}
            },
            Payload::MemorySection(_) => saw_memory = true,
            Payload::GlobalSection(_) => saw_global = true,
            Payload::DataSection(_) => saw_data = true,
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    assert!(saw_core);
    assert!(saw_modules);
    assert!(saw_instances);
    assert!(saw_stack);
    assert!(saw_memory);
    assert!(saw_global);
    assert!(saw_data);

use wasmi::{Config, Engine, Linker, Module, Store};
use wasmparser::{
    BinaryReader, CoreDumpInstancesSection, CoreDumpModulesSection, CoreDumpSection,
    CoreDumpStackSection, DataKind, GlobalType, Parser, Payload,
};

#[test]
fn coredump_sections_and_frames() {
    let mut config = Config::default();
    config.generate_coredump(true);
    config.coredump_executable_name("myexe");
    let engine = Engine::new(&config);
    let module = Module::new(
        &engine,
        r#"
        (module
            (memory (export "mem") 1)
            (global (export "g") i32 (i32.const 7))
            (func (export "trap") (param i32) (param i64) (param f32) (param f64) (local i32)
                local.get 0
                drop
                local.get 1
                drop
                local.get 2
                drop
                local.get 3
                drop
                i32.const 99
                local.set 4
                unreachable
            )
        )
        "#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());
    let linker = Linker::new(&engine);
    let instance = linker.instantiate_and_start(&mut store, &module).unwrap();
    let func = instance.get_typed_func::<(i32, i64, f32, f64), ()>(&store, "trap").unwrap();
    let error = func.call(&mut store, (42, -7, 1.5f32, -2.25f64)).unwrap_err();
    let coredump = error.coredump().expect("coredump should be present");

    let mut saw_core = false;
    let mut saw_modules = false;
    let mut saw_instances = false;
    let mut saw_stack = false;
    let mut saw_memory = false;
    let mut saw_global = false;
    let mut saw_data = false;

    for payload in Parser::new(0).parse_all(coredump) {
        let payload = payload.unwrap();
        match payload {
            Payload::CustomSection(reader) => match reader.name() {
                "core" => {
                    saw_core = true;
                    let data = reader.data();
                    let sec = CoreDumpSection::new(BinaryReader::new(data, 0)).unwrap();
                    assert_eq!(sec.name, "myexe");
                }
                "coremodules" => {
                    saw_modules = true;
                    let data = reader.data();
                    let sec = CoreDumpModulesSection::new(BinaryReader::new(data, 0)).unwrap();
                    assert_eq!(sec.modules.len(), 1);
                }
                "coreinstances" => {
                    saw_instances = true;
                    let data = reader.data();
                    let sec = CoreDumpInstancesSection::new(BinaryReader::new(data, 0)).unwrap();
                    assert_eq!(sec.instances.len(), 1);
                    let instance = &sec.instances[0];
                    assert_eq!(instance.module_index, 0);
                    assert_eq!(instance.memories, vec![0]);
                    assert_eq!(instance.globals, vec![0]);
                }
                "corestack" => {
                    saw_stack = true;
                    let data = reader.data();
                    let sec = CoreDumpStackSection::new(BinaryReader::new(data, 0)).unwrap();
                    assert_eq!(sec.name, "main");
                    assert_eq!(sec.frames.len(), 1);
                    let frame = &sec.frames[0];
                    assert_eq!(frame.instanceidx, 0);
                    assert_eq!(frame.funcidx, 0);
                    assert_eq!(frame.codeoffset, 0);
                    assert_eq!(frame.locals.len(), 5);
                    match frame.locals[0] {
                        wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::I32(v) => assert_eq!(v, 42),
                        _ => panic!("expected i32 local"),
                    }
                    match frame.locals[1] {
                        wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::I64(v) => assert_eq!(v, -7),
                        _ => panic!("expected i64 local"),
                    }
                    match frame.locals[2] {
                        wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::F32(v) => assert_eq!(v, 1.5),
                        _ => panic!("expected f32 local"),
                    }
                    match frame.locals[3] {
                        wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::F64(v) => assert_eq!(v, -2.25),
                        _ => panic!("expected f64 local"),
                    }
                    match frame.locals[4] {
                        wasmparser::CoreDumpValue::I32(v) => assert_eq!(v, 99),
                        _ => panic!("expected local i32"),
                    }
                }
                _ => {}
            },
            Payload::MemorySection(reader) => {
                saw_memory = true;
                let mems: Vec<_> = reader.into_iter().collect::<Result<_, _>>().unwrap();
                assert_eq!(mems.len(), 1);
                let ty = mems[0];
                assert_eq!(ty.minimum, 1);
                assert_eq!(ty.maximum, None);
                assert!(!ty.memory64);
            }
            Payload::GlobalSection(reader) => {
                saw_global = true;
                let globals: Vec<_> = reader
                    .into_iter()
                    .collect::<Result<Vec<_>, _>>()
                    .unwrap();
                assert_eq!(globals.len(), 1);
                let global = &globals[0];
                assert_eq!(global.ty, GlobalType {
                    val_type: wasmparser::ValType::I32,
                    mutable: false,
                    shared: false,
                });
            }
            Payload::DataSection(reader) => {
                saw_data = true;
                let data: Vec<_> = reader.into_iter().collect::<Result<_, _>>().unwrap();
                assert_eq!(data.len(), 1);
                match &data[0].kind {
                    DataKind::Active {
                        memory_index,
                        init_expr,
                    } => {
                        assert_eq!(*memory_index, 0);
                        let mut ops = init_expr.get_operators_reader();
                        let op = ops.read().unwrap();
                        match op {
                            wasmparser::Operator::I32Const { value } => assert_eq!(value, 0),
                            _ => panic!("expected i32.const 0 offset"),
                        }
                        assert_eq!(data[0].data.len(), 65536);
                    }
                    _ => panic!("expected active data segment"),
                }
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    assert!(saw_core);
    assert!(saw_modules);
    assert!(saw_instances);
    assert!(saw_stack);
    assert!(saw_memory);
    assert!(saw_global);
    assert!(saw_data);
}

use wasmi::{BinaryReader, Caller, Config, CoreDumpStackSection, Engine, Linker, Module, Store};

#[test]
fn coredump_includes_outer_frames_on_reentrancy() {
    let mut config = Config::default();
    config.generate_coredump(true);
    let engine = Engine::new(&config);

    // Inner module: traps when called.
    let inner_module = Module::new(
        &engine,
        r#"
        (module
            (func (export "inner") (param i32)
                local.get 0
                unreachable
            )
        )
        "#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    let mut store = Store::new(&engine, ());
    let inner_linker = Linker::new(&engine);
    let inner_instance = inner_linker
        .instantiate_and_start(&mut store, &inner_module)
        .unwrap();
    let inner = inner_instance
        .get_typed_func::<i32, ()>(&store, "inner")
        .unwrap();

    // Outer module: calls a host function which re-enters Wasm.
    let outer_module = Module::new(
        &engine,
        r#"
        (module
            (import "host" "callback" (func $callback (param i32)))
            (func (export "outer") (param i32)
                local.get 0
                call $callback
            )
        )
        "#,
    )
    .unwrap();

    let mut linker = Linker::new(&engine);
    let inner = std::sync::Arc::new(inner);
    let inner2 = inner.clone();
    linker.func_wrap("host", "callback", move |caller: Caller<'_, ()>, value: i32| {
        let inner = inner2.clone();
        inner.call(caller, value).map(|_| ())
    });
    let outer_instance = linker
        .instantiate_and_start(&mut store, &outer_module)
        .unwrap();
    let outer = outer_instance
        .get_typed_func::<i32, ()>(&store, "outer")
        .unwrap();

    let error = outer.call(&mut store, 5).unwrap_err();
    let coredump = error.coredump().expect("coredump should be present");
    let mut stack = None;
    for payload in wasmparser::Parser::new(0).parse_all(coredump) {
        let payload = payload.unwrap();
        if let wasmparser::Payload::CustomSection(reader) = payload {
            if reader.name() == "corestack" {
                stack = Some(
                    CoreDumpStackSection::new(BinaryReader::new(reader.data(), 0)).unwrap(),
                );
            }
        }
    }
    let stack = stack.expect("corestack section");
    assert_eq!(stack.frames.len(), 2, "expected inner and outer frames");
    // Youngest (inner) frame first, then outer frame.
    assert_ne!(
        stack.frames[0].instanceidx, stack.frames[1].instanceidx,
        "inner and outer frames should belong to different instances"
    );
    assert_eq!(stack.frames[0].funcidx, 0);
    assert_eq!(stack.frames[1].funcidx, 0);
}

Reentrant test passes. Now let me think about edge cases and correctness issues:

1. The active stack tracking uses a raw pointer to `StoreInner` in `ActiveStackGuard`. The guard is created in `execute_func` before execution and
dropped after. But when `execute_func` returns `Err` early (e.g., in `execute_func_resumable` when Host/OutOfFuel), the guard drops and pops. Good.
However, in `execute_func`, the guard is created and then `EngineExecutor::new(...).execute_root_func(...)` runs. If the execution returns an
`Err(ExecutionOutcome::Error(error))` with a coredump already attached, the guard drops at end of function. Fine.

But there's a critical issue: In `execute_func`, we create `_guard` then call `.execute_root_func(ctx.store, ...)`. But `ctx` is `StoreContextMut<T>`
and we already borrowed `&mut ctx.store.inner` to create the guard. The guard only stores a raw pointer, so the borrow ends. Then passing `ctx.store`
moves the `&mut Store<T>`. Fine.

However, in `execute_func_resumable`, when outcome is Host/OutOfFuel, the stack is moved into the resumable call object, and `_guard` drops at the
`return` — but wait, the guard is a local variable `_guard` in the function scope; it drops when the function returns (including the early `return
Ok(ResumableCallBase::HostTrap(...))`). The stack has been moved into `ResumableCallHostTrap` but the guard still holds the raw pointer and pops it
from active_stacks. That's correct: the stack is no longer active (suspended). When resumed, a new guard is created. Good.

2. The `generate` function accesses `state.store.inner()` and `state.code` and `state.stack`. But in `handle_trap`, `state` is `&mut VmState`.
`generate(state)` takes `&mut VmState`. Inside `generate`, `let store = state.store.inner();` borrows `state.store` immutably, and later uses
`state.code` and `state.stack` (via `active_stacks` and capture). Since `store` is used for the entire function (to resolve memories etc.), and
`state.stack` is accessed in capture_stack with `&*state.stack`? Actually `capture_stack(stack, store, &funcs)` where `stack` comes from `unsafe {
&*stack_ptr }` — not from `state.stack`! Wait, I removed the use of `state.stack`; frames are captured from `store.active_stacks()` raw pointers,
which include the innermost stack. So `state.stack` isn't used at all in generate. That avoids borrow issues. But is the innermost stack guaranteed to
be in `store.active_stacks()`? Yes, the guard was created for the innermost execution and pushed to the store's active_stacks. Good.

But there's a concern: `store` is `&StoreInner` derived from `state.store.inner()`. We then call `store.active_stacks()` which returns `&[*mut
Stack]`. Then we deref each pointer `&*stack_ptr`. The innermost pointer points to `state.stack` which is borrowed mutably by `state`. Creating a
shared ref via raw pointer while `state` holds `&mut Stack` is the aliasing concern discussed. The existing codebase uses `Inst` similarly. I'll
accept it.

Actually, can we avoid the unsafe for the innermost by using `&*state.stack`? But we don't know which pointer is innermost easily (it's the last). We
could do:
```rust
let stack_pointers = store.active_stacks();
// innermost is last; use state.stack for it to be safe
```
But we'd still deref outer pointers unsafely. The current approach is uniform. It's fine.
